post.summary: Create or resume a persistent account session
post.description: O-Kam account credentials are sent to vendor HTTPS services. The original password is not stored; the vendor protocol password digest and authorized session/transport credentials are saved in encrypted state for unattended recovery. Returns HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie and a Bearer session token for API clients. Protect both as secrets. If a bridge access token is configured, authenticate this request with Authorization: Bearer <bridge-access-token> (or Basic bridge:<token>); Compose web gateway supplies its private gateway header automatically. Sessions normally last one year; enabled publications retain their session. API restart restores sessions/cameras/publications. Explicit logout removes saved state.

post.summary: Start or reconnect camera over LAN or O-Kam cloud relay
post.description: Asynchronous. Poll camera state until viewable=true or error. Multiple lenses share one physical connection. LAN requires private network reachability; cloud uses vendor relay services and can require up to 100 seconds for the first frame. The chosen mode is persisted; existing publication URLs/passwords are retained across a source change. Cloud availability depends on vendor services, camera firmware and UDP reachability.

ip.description: Optional private IPv4 address; if omitted retain the saved LAN hint, then use account LAN IP or UID discovery. Not used for cloud routing.

connection_mode.description: LAN uses private IP/discovery; cloud requires vendor relay rendezvous by camera UID and ignores the LAN address for routing. No automatic fallback.

quality.description: Native quality command: high=1, medium=2, low=4. Null leaves existing quality untouched.

post.summary: Apply native stream preferences; change quality without reconnecting
post.description: On an already connected camera with unchanged transport/IP/substream, applies native quality over the serialized existing session and persists it without replacing the camera or publication. A changed mode, LAN IP, substream or disconnected camera starts asynchronous connection instead. Cloud does not use IP for routing. Response mode is live or reconnect. Null clears the saved override without changing the current native quality. Native quality is shared by all lenses; a brief keyframe/encoder transition is possible.

post.summary: Send a validated native camera action
post.description: Requires a connected viewable camera. Commands execute serially in its existing native session. state=confirmed means result=0; sent means transport delivery only; rejected carries firmware result. Queue timeouts never execute later. Commands can change persistent settings; call only intentionally. Action definitions and parameter ranges are in x-actions. Image ranges: brightness/contrast 0..255, orientation 0..3, night 0..2. plaintext_password configures documented ExUserSwitch external access; it does not prove ONVIF/RTSP services exist. Verify get_params + independent service probe afterwards.

post.description: Requires connected camera. Publishes original H264 for observed lenses over RTSP/TCP; ONVIF exposes Device/Media, bounded PTZ when a motor is reported, PullPoint events from actual native observations, and Recording/Search/Replay for completed server/SD-cache clips. No native camera settings are changed. Active publication keeps the camera and owning account session alive; closing a browser tab does not stop it. Logout, explicit disconnect or disabling publication stops it. Server restart restores desired publication with the same paths and credentials. Enabling extends the account cookie lifetime while publication is active. No ONVIF certification, absolute positioning, reverse playback or events inferred from video are claimed.

post.summary: Control server recording, import SD clip or start forward replay
post.description: Requires an enabled bridge publication. record explicitly starts/stops H264-copy server recording. sd_import uses only an identifier from sd_records, returns an asynchronous job, downloads at most 300 seconds and 500 MiB in a separate authenticated camera session; no SD files are deleted. replay returns RTSP URI for a completed private recording. Credentials are the current publication credentials. Server retention/quota policy is persisted per account/camera; SD cache shares quota but is not aged out using its original camera date. At most two SD download jobs run globally; 2 GiB free space required before import. File playback is forward at normal speed, not arbitrary reverse or clock-range seeking.
